message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the most recent common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (the cats) and **Perissodactyla** (the odd‑toed ungulates such as horses, rhinos, and zebras).  

In other words, it is the last common ancestor of the clade that contains all placental mammals (Eutheria). That ancestor lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleocene, and would have been a small, insect‑eating mammal—far removed from the large, specialized predators and grazers we see today.
